source.title: HABITAT-VERTICAL-001: co-design factory, product, and end-to-end supply chain for repairable household goods
source.body:
## Mission

Extend [SLEEP-PRODUCT-001 #8039](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/8039) from an excellent product concept to an evidence-bearing **factory-to-product vertical**: upstream materials and suppliers, conversion, components, assembly, quality, utilities, workforce, facility design, distribution, repair/refurbishment and material recovery.

The intended paradigm shift is product–process–factory–supply-chain co-design. Do not optimize a mattress topper, furniture article or garment in isolation and only afterward discover that its materials, tools, factory layout, labor model, energy/water needs, transport, repair path or economics make it infeasible.

This issue is an integration / benchmark profile. It is **not** a new generic MRP/ERP, scheduling engine, process semantics, factory ontology, material registry, inventory ledger, digital twin, commissioning engine, or execution-authority system.

## Existing owners to compose (avoid duplication)

- Symthaea **MFG-PROC-000 #5686** and its children: process identity, process capability, recipe, process plan, pre/postconditions, manufacturability and process qualification.
- Symthaea **MFG-LIFE-000 #5705**: lifecycle/circularity projection.
- Symthaea **BUILT-ENV-001 #6032**, **BUILT-CX-001 #6037**, **BUILT-BIM-001 #6036**, **BUILT-SITE-001 #6034**, **BUILT-ROB-PILOT-001 #6040**: site/facility/workcell realization, commissioning, model exchange and low-risk demonstrator.
- Symthaea **FACTORY-OPS-001 #7677**: reuse the existing capability-constrained deterministic scheduling direction; do not create a second operations-research scheduler.
- Symthaea **ENG-DESIGN-001 #6005**, **ENG-DESIGN-003 #6091**, **ENG-MAT/materials**, structural, thermal/thermofluids, equipment, energy, water, metrology, reliability and safety owners as applicable.
- Mycelix **MFG-EVID-001 #3084** and **MFG-PROC-001 #3085**: design revisions/BOM-to-unit evidence, supplier/resource offers, routings/work orders, production and lot genealogy.
- Mycelix **LOG-COMMONS-001 #4900** and existing Supply Chain / Manufacturing functions: federated logistics and participant-owned operational/provenance facts.
- Mycelix carries operational events and multi-party provenance; Symthaea owns engineering meaning, analysis and scoped qualification. No cross-project claim may silently promote an offer, plan, signature, simulation or event into physical capability or product qualification.

## Initial vertical: human-habitat goods

First use the modular mattress topper from #8039, with two follow-on product profiles:
1. a flat-pack desk or storage unit;
2. one repairable everyday garment / workwear item.

Keep the first physical pilot to a low-risk, small-scale textile/converting-and-assembly cell. Furniture and garment cases may initially be synthetic process/fixture cases until their dedicated material and product-function evidence exists. The common vertical contract should accommodate all three without pretending that mattress comfort, furniture strength and garment fit are interchangeable.

## End-to-end value chain to represent

Use exact identified stages and evidence-bearing transitions; do not let existence of an upstream material claim establish downstream product capability.

```
demand / user requirements / product variants
-> product architecture + design revision + test requirements
-> bill of materials + process plan + manufacturing capability demands
-> upstream raw/secondary feedstocks and supplier claims
-> material processing / grade qualification
-> fabric / cover / layer / panel / fastener / component production
-> inbound logistics, lot receipt, inspection and quarantine/acceptance
-> workcell routing, labor/tools/equipment and production plan
-> transformation, assembly and intermediate inspection/hold/rework
-> final article identity + acceptance/quality evidence
-> packaging, storage, outbound transport and delivery
-> use, maintenance, replacement parts and repair
-> return triage, refurbishment/remanufacture/reuse
-> material recovery with actual route/grade evidence or disposal
-> observed demand/defect/repair/recovery feedback into redesign
```

Every transformation must retain input identities, material state/grade, quantity and unit semantics, process profile/revision, facility/equipment/workcell identity, responsible execution evidence, inspection observations, outputs/yield/scrap/byproducts, and uncertainty where relevant. A process plan is not an executed process; a completed operation is not an accepted article; recyclability is not recovered feedstock.

## Factory design scope

Create an evidence-bound reference-design profile for an SME-scale, modular microfactory/workshop. Do not start with an expensive, fully autonomous "lights-out" factory. Compare manual, assisted, and appropriately automated layouts where all have the same stated demand, quality, staffing, and safety requirements.

The factory model should include:

- Site and facility: site/geotechnical applicability references; spatial layout; receiving, quarantine, storage, workcells, inspection, finished goods, repair/returns and waste/recovery zones; access, egress and expansion constraints.
- Utilities: electrical demand and quality, thermal conditioning, ventilation/dust extraction where needed, lighting, water and wastewater if process-relevant, data/communications, compressed air if justified, backup/common-mode dependency assumptions.
- Equipment/workcell: exact equipment and tool identities, capability envelope, process/material applicability, maintenance/calibration status, cycle/setup time distributions or bounded ranges, changeover and inspection needs.
- Material flow: travel distance/time, handling damage, WIP buffers, storage conditions, lot segregation, ergonomic handling, packaging and reverse flows.
- Workforce: required skills, training pathways, accessible workstations, workload and ergonomic constraints; no optimization that treats injury exposure, worker dignity or legal labor obligations as a compensable cost.
- Environment and safety: domain-appropriate guarding, fire/egress, dust/noise/chemical exposure, occupational safety and building-code review; these must be supplied by qualified owners/professionals, not guessed from a digital layout.
- Facility lifecycle: commissioning, observation, maintenance, calibration, repair, change impact and recommissioning. Installed, powered or successfully started is not the same as commissioned under requirements.
- Local capability and sourcing: separate local labor/value-added, locally available commodity inputs, imported specialty materials/parts, single points of failure and recovery options; do not equate "assembled locally" with full local supply-chain closure.

A site/factory simulation may compare candidate layouts and utility profiles, but does not grant permit, construction, safety, commissioning, or equipment execution authority.

## Proposed benchmark framework

All numbers below are **proposed target directions**, not current results or universal industry thresholds. Freeze metric definitions, data boundaries and baselines before interpreting outcomes.

### 1. Traceability and qualification integrity
- 100% of selected critical inputs in the pilot must link from received supplier lot through process/inspection events to the finished article or explicitly recorded scrap/rework.
- Every output must bind exact product revision, BOM, process-plan revision, material lots, workcell profile and disposition.
- 100% of deliberately unknown, stale, unqualified or mismatched critical prerequisites must be blocked from a qualified-pass state.
- Target recall/containment query: identify all affected units from a seeded input-lot fault in under 5 minutes on the bounded pilot corpus; report corpus size and hardware/runtime.
- Track supplier substitution, source license/specification, freshness and approval as independent fields.

### 2. Production flow and economic performance
- Establish baselines for end-to-end lead time, touch time, queue time, setup/changeover, WIP, first-pass yield, rework, scrap, delivered cost and on-time-in-full delivery.
- Benchmark deterministic scheduling against a simple documented baseline for the same orders, skills, resource capacities and calendars. Feasibility must be exact; optimization quality can be measured separately.
- Target a 20% reduction in delivered cost versus a named functional reference for the selected product where feasible. Include materials, yield loss, labor, consumables, depreciation/capacity allocation, QA, maintenance/spares, energy, water where applicable, packaging, freight, returns, tax/duty and replacement burden. Publish assumptions and sensitivity.
- Proposed pilot improvement gate after a valid measured baseline: reduce order lead time or WIP by 15–20% without worsening safety, quality, worker loading or service level. If the synthetic model alone shows improvement, label it a simulation result and validate it physically later.

### 3. Resource use and environmental performance
- Report metered or explicitly modeled energy per accepted functional unit; distinguish idle/base load, process energy and facility utilities.
- Report process-water withdrawal/consumption and wastewater only where applicable; do not invent a water benefit for a dry process.
- Track input mass, accepted output, scrap, rework, packaging, byproducts and recovered material mass with an explicit balance and measurement uncertainty.
- Compare lifecycle impact only with a declared ISO 14040/14044-compatible goal/scope, functional unit, boundary, allocation choices, data quality and sensitivity. Never infer environmental superiority from a recycled-content percentage alone.
- Target at least 15% lower energy per accepted unit from a frozen baseline as an exploration goal, not a release requirement until metering and quality equivalence are shown.

### 4. Facility and resilience
- Compare layouts on material travel, throughput, ergonomic exposure, egress/access, inspection separation, utility demand, changeover flexibility and space for repair/recovery flows.
- Run supply/operations stress cases: a critical supplier lot rejection, alternate supplier with different lead time/grade, machine outage, power interruption, water interruption if relevant, workforce-skill absence, transport disruption, and demand mix change.
- Quantify lost output, backlog, recovery time, service impact and cost for each disruption. Do not use a vague "resilience score" without declared scenarios.
- Show that a modular cell can add/remove a workcell or change product mix without corrupting lineage, qualification or resource-capability claims.
- Commissioning and operational qualification remain separate gates; a planned factory layout is not a commissioned factory.

### 5. Maintenance, workforce and circularity
- Track planned/unplanned downtime, maintenance time, calibration expiry, spare-part lead time, time-to-diagnose and repair, training time and skills coverage.
- Target replacement of the common wear component within the product-specific benchmark, with documented tools/parts and trained-operator conditions.
- Quantify jobs/skill hours and ergonomic risk indicators without reducing human flourishing to simple throughput per worker.
- Report return triage, repair/refurbishment yield, product/component reuse, material recovery and disposal separately. Count recovery only when a real route accepts that material grade and condition.
- Include a training and operator-feedback loop; workers must be able to stop, challenge or annotate a plan without retaliation encoded into the software.

## Machine-readable benchmark corpus and hostile controls

The first synthetic corpus should include at least:

1. Valid single supplier → receiving inspection → fabric/cover preparation → sewing/assembly → inspection → accepted article.
2. Exact upstream input lot exists but actual delivered grade is unverified.
3. Substitute supplier has the same marketing name but a different grade/process envelope.
4. A material transformation is marked completed with no required observation; downstream qualification is blocked.
5. A rejected lot contaminates multiple WIP/final units; containment enumerates exactly affected descendants and does not falsely recall unrelated units.
6. Machine/tool says it can perform the process but its qualification, calibration or availability is stale.
7. Scheduler plan omits a required skill, resource or inspection hold point.
8. Queue/setup/cycle data missing but an optimizer reports a precise completion date.
9. Price excludes scrap/yield loss, labor, utilities, freight or returns.
10. Low-carbon/recycled input has unknown provenance, grade or upstream burden; environmental claim stays unresolved.
11. Nominally recyclable multi-material construction has no regionally available recovery route.
12. Factory layout appears feasible while ventilation, emergency egress, guarding or accessibility evidence is absent.
13. Power interruption affects both primary production and inspection/calibration; model must surface the common mode.
14. Product revision changes a seam/layer/fastener/process and stale qualification cannot carry forward.
15. Supplier or carrier cannot share sensitive commercial details; preserve minimum provenance commitments and access control without fabricating data.
16. Repair returns arrive but no capacity/spare part exists; "repairable by design" does not become "repair completed".
17. Mycelix inventory or signed delivery event conflicts with a physical receiving measurement; preserve both source events and an unresolved discrepancy.
18. A complete synthetic path is reported correctly as synthetic-only, never actual production capability.

## Interoperability and external research anchors

Use standards as external mappings and test-method references; do not make an external standard the sole internal identity or assume the pilot is certified.

- [ISA-95 / IEC 62264](https://www.isa.org/standards-and-publications/isa-standards/isa-95-standard): enterprise/logistics to manufacturing operations/control interfaces and vocabulary. Current ISA page includes ANSI/ISA-95.00.01-2025.
- [ISO 22400-1](https://www.iso.org/cms/%20render/live/en/sites/isoorg/contents/data/standard/05/68/56847.html) / [ISO 22400-2](https://www.iso.org/standard/54497.html): manufacturing-operations KPI concepts and formulas; ISO/DIS 22400-2 is under development, so pin the edition actually used.
- [NIST Digital Thread for Manufacturing](https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/digital-thread-manufacturing): product definition, manufacturing, inspection and measured result linkage.
- [GS1 Global Traceability Standard](https://www.gs1.org/standards/gs1-global-traceability-standard/current-standard): traceability goals, object IDs, batch/lot versus instance-level identity.
- [ISO 50001](https://www.iso.org/standard/69426.html): energy management framework.
- [ISO 14040](https://www.iso.org/standard/37456.html): lifecycle assessment principles and framework.
- [EU ESPR Regulation (EU) 2024/1781](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/eng) and [European Commission DPP working plan/FAQ](https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/single-market/digital-product-passport/explore-our-faqs_en): model/batch/item-level product data, open interoperable data and product-group-specific implementation. The Commission's 2 July 2026 plan puts textiles in the 2027 workstream, furniture in 2028, and mattresses in 2029; these are planned rule-adoption windows, not proof that every product already requires a DPP.

For an initial South African/regionally adaptable pilot, keep site-, electricity-, water-, labor-, freight-, standards- and supplier-specific assumptions explicit and replaceable. Do not hard-code a US/EU factory model as universal. Before physical implementation, a locally qualified engineering team must review actual zoning, building/fire/occupational-safety requirements, electrical compliance, environmental permits and applicable product standards.

## Execution sequence and acceptance criteria

1. Freeze the exact consumer product candidate, comparable baseline, BOM/material identities, supplier geography, lot rules, production demand, shift/calendar, skill/resource capabilities, test/inspection gates and unit/currency basis.
2. Publish one small synthetic supply-chain + factory manifest that links supplier-lot events to a workcell/process DAG, inspections, product disposition, cost/resource metrics and end-of-life path.
3. Define deterministic calculations and an independent, stdlib-only Rust qualifier using the existing manufacturing contracts/operations-research owners if their exact public API is qualified and usable. Do not implement a second scheduler or manufacturing state machine.
4. Freeze expected outputs and negative-control receipts before running candidate comparisons.
5. Report exactly which contract/corpus tests were run, on which source heads, plus pass/fail and skipped explicitly. A queued/skipped runner is never a pass.
6. Only after synthetic qualification should a low-risk physical pilot be staged: incoming-lot tagging, textile cutting/sewing or cover assembly, low-energy handling, calibrated dimensional/weight checks, and manual operator sign-off. Do not introduce autonomous high-risk equipment or hazardous processing.
7. Plan the factory layout and utility studies through BUILT-ENV/BUILT-CX/BUILT-ROB-PILOT and qualified engineers; no floorplan simulation acts as permission to construct or operate.
8. Publish a reusable follow-on mapping for repairable furniture and clothing, with product-specific tests and safety/legal owners.

## Claim ceiling

Opening this work establishes an architecture and benchmark plan only. It does not establish physical supply, qualified suppliers, product quality, factory readiness, local self-sufficiency, cost competitiveness, environmental superiority, compliance, worker safety, or production capability. Synthetic and modeled outputs remain distinct from measured and independently replicated facts.

comments.text: Implementation starter: draft PR https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/pull/8053 adds the factory-to-product vertical contract and synthetic benchmark fixture. The fixture is synthetic-only; its JSON parsing, process predecessor/resource/skill consistency, and acyclic operation graph were checked at head `fd76d3dbe11595a001b0249da7c0bfc00431e832`. Exact-head CI/workflow records are skipped, not pass. No physical factory/product claims are made.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text:
Integration note: I opened [Symtropy CIRC-MFG-001 #1984](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/1984) and draft [PR #1986](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/pull/1986), now deliberately scoped to the construction-specific evidence contract used by this wider factory/product/supply-chain vertical.

This should remain a consumer/reference profile, not a second ontology, MRP/ERP, lifecycle database or optimizer. Mycelix owns BOM/work-order and lifecycle/custody event references; Symtropy #1596 owns its housing evidence/jurisdiction boundary; your HABITAT vertical should own product/factory/supply-chain co-design and its demonstration; MFG-VALUE #7608 remains the owner of production-value comparisons.

Suggested integration experiment after the contract gate is qualified: pick one low-risk, non-load-bearing modular service enclosure or panel kit, freeze the product and process identity, and measure end-to-end material inputs, conforming outputs, rework, assembly/service time, transport, repair, disassembly damage and independently accepted reuse. Treat all 10% improvement targets as preregistered hypotheses, not claims.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text:
Follow-up from the current [Symtropy CIRC-MFG-001 draft](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/pull/1986): I have made the synthetic cross-system binding explicit across four owners. The current fixture roles include a Symthaea process-plan reference, Mycelix process/accounting/custody references, a Symtropy qualification reference, and a Sol-Atlas site-resource observation. The authority/role assignments are integration hypotheses in synthetic data, not claims that any real artifact is already available or qualified.

The new adversarial controls include missing Sol-Atlas site-resource evidence and the same local reference ID under the wrong owning authority. This keeps a missing or ambiguous water/energy/access observation from being silently promoted to site capacity. The reference harness does not duplicate your factory/product/supply-chain model or the production-value evaluator.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text: Further progress is in draft PR #8053: `symthaea-habitat-vertical-bench` now includes exact integer-based synthetic delivered-cost and material-balance oracles in addition to fixture/lot-genealogy validation. The fixture's two cost totals recompute to 250,000 and 210,000 synthetic minor units; candidate/reference ratio is 8,400 basis points (84%), correctly above the proposed 80% ceiling. The synthetic mass stream closes at 100% with 85% accepted-mass yield. These are arithmetic known answers only—not actual prices or production outcomes. 31 Rust tests are authored but not compiled or run here; exact-head workflows are skipped, not pass.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text: Latest PR #8053 update at exact head `12f79470f94069754d29febeebd485ebeb9aa008`: the Rust scaffold now adds two more auditable arithmetic contracts: a 12-category delivered-cost known answer using checked integer sums/exact ratio comparison, and a single-stream material-balance known answer with residual/tolerance/closure. Synthetic cost ratio is 84%, correctly NOT meeting the proposed 80% target; synthetic material closure is 100%, accepted-mass yield 85%. Fixture preflight independently matched all four lot-containment descendant sets and found no duplicate IDs, unknown graph endpoints, cycles, or unresolved process/skill refs. 31 Rust tests are authored but remain uncompiled/unexecuted; one workflow is in progress and other checks are skipped, not pass. No physical claims are made.

comments.text:
## Continuation update — paired disruption campaign

Added to the existing HABITAT-VERTICAL-001 draft PR rather than opening a parallel scheduler/benchmark engine:

- Campaign contract: https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/blob/research/habitat-vertical-001-factory-supply-chain/docs/research/HABITAT_COUNTERFACTUAL_001_DISRUPTION_CAMPAIGN.md
- Machine-readable eight-case campaign: https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/blob/research/habitat-vertical-001-factory-supply-chain/docs/research/fixtures/habitat-vertical-scenarios-v0.1.json
- Rust definition-only qualifier: https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/blob/research/habitat-vertical-001-factory-supply-chain/crates/domains/symthaea-habitat-vertical-bench/src/scenario_campaign.rs

Static JSON preflight found exact source coverage for all 8 declared disruptions, identical required-output lists, valid metric references, explicit execution blockers, zero embedded numeric results, and baseline/candidate policies still unbound. The qualifier adds 13 Rust unit tests (44 authored across this crate), but none have been compiled or executed. At inspected HEAD `bbfdc99eb6c35d6292d5ec3037cf32315dbd994d`, the compare is 39 commits ahead / 0 behind and all 8 observed workflow records are completed/skipped; no passing workflow is claimed.

Research grounding: NIST's manufacturing digital-twin guidance calls for credible verification/validation, quantified uncertainty, interoperability and trustworthy models; GS1 EPCIS offers an existing interoperable supply-chain event vocabulary. These are interface/test anchors, not validation of this implementation:
- https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/digital-twins-advanced-manufacturing
- https://www.nist.gov/publications/manufacturing-digital-twin-standards
- https://www.gs1.org/standards/epcis

New proposed hypothesis, not an achieved result: after exact baseline/candidate policies, runnable cases, units and horizon are pinned, aim for >=10% lower lost accepted-unit-hours across runnable paired cases with zero hard-gate violations; retain all case-wise results and NotEvaluable/Blocked states. Demand-mix change and repair-spare shortage remain not evaluable until the variant BOM/setup model and repair inventory/capacity profile exist.

comments.text:
## Additional continuation — resilience option-value benchmark

Added a synthetic-only option-value benchmark to the existing HABITAT-VERTICAL-001 PR, linked to current robust-decision owners instead of duplicating an optimizer.

- Contract: https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/blob/ca10122ab3ca9a3e388e2afa64d7d28f5317f87e/docs/research/HABITAT_RESILIENCE_OPTIONS_001_OPTION_VALUE.md
- Six options × eight existing disruptions = 48 synthetic outcome cells: https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/blob/ca10122ab3ca9a3e388e2afa64d7d28f5317f87e/docs/research/fixtures/habitat-resilience-options-v0.1.json
- Rust validator and 13 authored adversarial tests: https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/blob/ca10122ab3ca9a3e388e2afa64d7d28f5317f87e/crates/domains/symthaea-habitat-vertical-bench/src/resilience_options.rs

Static JSON preflight confirms six options, eight exact source disruption IDs, all 48 option/scenario pairs unique, qualification gates on every option, valid intervals, localized mitigation behavior, no ungrounded scenario probabilities/ROI, and no real-qualification claims. These are deliberately constructed algorithmic challenge values, not operational estimates. The evaluator refuses to choose a robust winner: interval-frontier/minimax-regret APIs and real option/policy revisions remain unbound.

Research grounding added from current NIST work on digital-twin VVUQ/interoperability, the 2026 smart-manufacturing AI/ML roadmap, and September 2026 circular-manufacturing systems research. See the linked contract for sources and scope limits.

Exact head `ca10122ab3ca9a3e388e2afa64d7d28f5317f87e` is 49 commits ahead / 0 behind, 14 changed files. There are 57 authored Rust test functions in this crate; none has been compiled or executed. All eight observed workflows at the exact head are completed/skipped, not passing. PR remains draft.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text:
## Resilience-option continuation: exact-head status

Follow-up validation/hardening is complete on the current draft branch:
- Latest inspected head: `8729d9907cc348a1692270a7efb4f995e0038924`
- Compare against main: 50 commits ahead, 0 behind; 14 changed files.
- Fixture static preflight: 6 option concepts × 8 source scenarios = 48 exact unique cells; all options carry qualification gates; scenario IDs exactly match the paired-disruption campaign; intervals are ordered; all outcomes are synthetic-only; mitigations affect only declared scenarios; no probability or ROI model was added.
- Rust source: 57 authored test functions across the structural/accounting, scenario-campaign, and option-value modules. None has been compiled or executed here. Tests and CLI wiring are authored, not passing evidence.
- Exact-head workflows currently mix `in_progress` with `completed / skipped`. No PASS is claimed and work did not wait on them.
- Robust frontier/minimax regret is intentionally not run; exact canonical API revisions and strategy qualifications remain unbound.

The important next engineering gate remains adapter/ownership verification for SE-OPT #7788, ICCB-004 #8024, MFG-VALUE-001 #7608, and FACTORY-OPS-001 #7677. We should consume these owners rather than add another optimizer or scheduler.
